entities.summary: Upo Wetland (Korean: 우포늪) is a complex of natural wetlands located in Changnyeong County, South Gyeongsang Province, South Korea. It is located in portions of Yueo-myeon, Ibang-myeon and Daehap-myeon, near the Nakdong River. It derives its name from the largest of the wetlands, Upo. Other wetlands in the complex include Mokpo, Sajipo and Jjokjibeol wetlands. The complex as a whole covers 2.13 km2, and is the largest inland wetland in South Korea today. It is one of eight Ramsar wetlands in the country and one of the official visiting sites for the 10th Meeting of the Conference of the Contracting Parties that was held in Changwon, Korea in October, 2008.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Upo Wetland is significant as it is one of eight Ramsar wetlands in South Korea, covering an area of 2.13 km2 and serving as a habitat for various plant and animal species. Its designation as a protected site has helped preserve the region's biodiversity.
